text:
Aisha (support): Lina reporting customers seeing bursty 429s on Dedicated this morning, started ~08:12 UTC. Saying long chat sessions (40k+ tokens) correlate with the spike.

Lina (customer): yes, we see a pile of 429s and higher tail latency after a big import job created long sessions. Happened 08:10-08:30. Here are a couple request IDs: req_01f, req_01g.

Aisha (support): thanks — can you share an obfuscated request sample and whether you were using pinned model version or a fallback?

Lina (customer): pinned to rwd-3b-v2, single dedicated pool. sample payload: `{
  "prompt": "<long context of 35k tokens>...",
  "max_tokens": 1024
}`

Aisha (support): tagging Dan + Ryan to investigate KV cache memory pressure + autoscale behavior on the dedicated pool.

Dan (sre): looking at infra metrics now. I see sustained kvcache memory usage with fragmentation spikes and repeated slab reclaim attempts around 08:12. Node-level alloc failures from jemalloc occasionally.

Ryan (runtime): that aligns with runtime traces — heavy KV growth from longcontext sessions causing large prefix KV entries. We try to coalesce but fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation for new slabs so eviction thrash begins.

Dan (sre): logs (excerpt):
```
[08:12:14] kvcache: alloc failed; requested 18446744071562067968 bytes
[08:12:15] slab: compaction started; freed 12MB
[08:12:18] eviction: candidate eviction wave size=128; evicted=124; backpressure=true
[08:12:20] autoscaler: scale_out_trigger ignored because recent_scale=yes
```

Aisha (support): autoscaler ignored scale out? autoscale-bot, can you paste policy state?

autoscale-bot: policy "dedicated-default" cooldown active: last_scaled 00:03:21 ago; max_scale_limit=5; current_replicas=3; queued_scale_requests=2

Ryan (runtime): autoscaling cooldown plus fragmentation means we had room to add GPU but the allocator couldn't place new cache structures; runtime applied QOS backpressure -> 429s for new incoming requests to protect in-flight long contexts.

Lina (customer): So that's why requests kept failing despite free GPUs?

Dan (sre): yes. The memory looked free at OS level but the runtime's slab allocator had fragmentation and small free chunks; compaction isn't aggressive enough during sustained long-key workloads.

Aisha (support): repro steps we used in cluster: loadgen with longprefix sequences, 10 concurrent sessions, each appending 2k tokens per minute for 10 minutes. Command: `loadgen --endpoint https://dedicated.rwd/api/generate --concurrency 10 --payload-file longctx.json --tps 6`

Ryan (runtime): mitigation options we tried: 1) rollout of a slab compaction tweak to be more aggressive on fragmentation thresholds; 2) enable per-tenant KV TTL (evict older prefixes sooner); 3) temporarily reduce max_context for that pool; 4) bump reserved heap for kvcache via config `kvcache.reserved_bytes=1.5GB`.

Dan (sre): short-term action: we scaled the pool to 5 replicas and applied a rolling restart with compaction patch -> immediate drop in eviction thrash and 429s subsided within ~90s. Rolling restart explanation: restart allows allocator to rebuild contiguous arenas, which reduced allocation failures.

Aisha (support): Lina — we applied 2 and 4 as a safety net for your tenant: set per-tenant kv_ttl=15m and increased reserved_bytes. Can you confirm whether errors stopped for you?

Lina (customer): errors dropped dramatically, tail latency back to normal. Appreciate the quick action.

Ryan (runtime): longer-term action items: - tune compaction to trigger earlier under long-prefix workloads - introduce a fragmentation metric and alert (fragmentation_ratio > 0.7) - add an autoscaler override when fragmentation prevents allocation so we can force add capacity and avoid cooldown ignoring critical events - improve eviction policy to prioritize very large prefixes to avoid single long session taking whole slab

Dan (sre): ops playbook updates: add a diagnostic runbook: `rwd debug kvcache --pool dedicated-xy --sample-requests` which captures slab map, fragmentation heatmap, top prefixes by size, and jemalloc stats.

Aisha (support): next steps for customer: we'll keep kv_ttl at 15m for 48h, monitor fragment_ratio and eviction_wave_count. I'll follow up after 24h with telemetry.

Lina (customer): thanks — please include the request IDs if anything spikes again.

Ryan (runtime): saved repro artifacts in /var/log/repro/3109876543/ (s3 link redacted) and a patch candidate ready: PR#4123 (compaction tuning).

Dan (sre): owners assigned: runtime=Ryan, autoscale=Dan, support lead=Aisha. Setting alert: `kvcache_fragment_ratio > 0.7` => paging oncall.

Aisha (support): marking resolved for now but keeping this thread open for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
